what: When a quick run is followed within about a minute by a full run on the same commit, which the new build instructions ask for after the last ticket, the hand-over page blames a browser test that failed with the others in the quick run on the full run as well, and says it happened in both runs. In the same case, when the full run's own record of flaky tests is missing (for example because its browser tests were stopped at their time limit), the page does not say the record is missing, because it takes the quick run's record line for the full run's. I showed both with a script on hand-made records: a quick run ending at 10:00:00 and a full run of 3.7 minutes ending at 10:04:02 both claim the record line written at 09:59:58. The cause is that the page matches a record line to a run when it was written on the same commit at any time within the whole run's length plus a minute before the run ended, although the browser tests run last and write their line seconds before the run ends, so the window reaches back into the run before.

A pull request that renames a file that judges it out of the way (pytest.ini to pytest.ini.off, or checks.py to another name) gets no notice at all, and one that renames a test file so its tests are no longer collected (tests/test_app.py to tests/app_checks_off.py) is counted as removing no tests. I ran both against a temporary git repository with the notice script: the run's summary stayed empty. The cause is that git's rename detection, on by default, reports a renamed file under its new name only and with no removed lines, and the notice looks only at the new names and at removed lines.

The repo notes tell an agent to give a whole run of the checks a fifteen-minute timeout, and the skill edit written out for the owner says the same, but the agent's command tool allows at most ten minutes for a command it waits on, so an agent that follows the first half of the instruction either has the command refused or stops waiting at ten minutes while a slow run can take up to thirteen, and then reports no result. The cause is that the new waiting time was set from the new limits alone without the tool's own ten-minute ceiling; only running the checks in the background fits a run that can last thirteen minutes.

The hand-over script, one of the files to be copied into the starter kit, names one of this product's browser tests in an example: "A filter reaches the registry" for test_a_filter_reaches_the_registry. The spec asks that none of the changed loop files name anything of this product. The cause is the example chosen for the new function that turns a browser test's name into words.
